answer: I used the garnet default calibration set f81c45da-6e73-4b5d-a0fe-72c75635fade. It has 28 CZ pairs, and every pair has a valid IRB fidelity for the default slepian_crf implementation (metrics.irb.cz.slepian_crf.<pair>.fidelity:par=d2). The best chain is QB7-QB12-QB11, with QB12 in the middle. The IRB CZ fidelity of QB7-QB12 is 0.998016 and of QB12-QB11 is 0.998693. Their product is 0.996712. The next best chain is QB16-QB11-QB12, with a product of 0.994689. I ran the GHZ circuit on garnet:mock with 200 shots. It puts H on QB12, then CX from QB12 to QB7 and from QB12 to QB11. The transpiler mapped these to physical indices 6, 11 and 10 and used no routing. The transpiled circuit has exactly 2 CZ gates, on QB12-QB7 and QB12-QB11, and it measures all 3 qubits. Job 01a15fa4-3c13-7511-8aca-122f673084f6 returned {'111': 51, '000': 45, '011': 50, '100': 54}. Qiskit bit order is little-endian with c0=QB7, c1=QB12 and c2=QB11. The mock gives random results, so these counts do not show a real GHZ state. The scripts are in /Users/claytonchancey/Desktop/quantum/.claude/worktrees/wf_3612af23-e49-107/scratch/.
